## claude.ai entire-prod-us
Entire MCP — an investigation surface over Entire's engineering data: repos and their analytics, git history (commits, files, trees, refs, diffs), the AI checkpoints and sessions behind the code (with transcripts and token accounting), trails (PR-like change proposals), and code search. Reads are curated `*_entire` tools; a small write/ops group covers trail/review/runner/dispatch mutations.

Workflow: when you only have a repo name, path, or URL, call resolve_entire_repo first, then pass the repo it returns to repo-scoped tools. Prefer the aggregation tools (get_entire_repo_overview, get_entire_my_activity) over hand-rolling stats from raw listings.

Querying conventions (shared by every tool):
- Addressing: name a repo by a prefixed path (gh/<owner>/<repo>, et/<project>/<repo>, git/<owner>/<repo>) or a repo ULID. Repo ULIDs are REGION-SCOPED — the same repo has a different ULID per region, so never carry a ULID across regions or sessions; if a tool rejects one, re-resolve with resolve_entire_repo.
- Pagination: every list takes an opaque cursor and returns next_cursor when more remains — exhaust the pages before concluding "that's all".
- Time: since/until are ISO 8601 / RFC3339 bounds; where offered, timeframe is a relative window (last-month, last-3-months, last-6-months).
- Size: reads that can be large (files, diffs, transcripts) honor max_tokens and return next_cursor to continue — raise max_tokens or page rather than assuming truncation is the whole story.

Pitfalls:
- sessions[].tokenUsage on a checkpoint is a PER-CHECKPOINT delta, not a session total — sum across a session's checkpoints, or use get_entire_session for the authoritative total.
- list_entire_checkpoints silently truncates older history; for a branch's COMPLETE checkpoint membership, paginate list_entire_commits and collect the per-commit checkpoint IDs.

Skills: before deep work in a domain, load the matching skill (list_entire_skills / load_entire_skill) — entire/checkpoints-and-sessions and entire/token-analysis before token accounting, … [truncated]

## claude.ai incident.io
The incident.io MCP server lets you query and manage incidents, alerts, escalations, schedules, follow-ups, catalog data, and telemetry.

If another connected MCP server exposes an incident_pin tool (alongside incident_list, incident_show, etc.), that is the incident.io desktop server — prefer it for every incident.io action. It is a superset of this one: it proxies these same tools and adds local-only capabilities (the user's pinned incident, locally-cached investigations, opening links). Don't split a task across both servers — in particular, an ask / ask_incident / ask_telemetry session_id from this server is not valid on the desktop server, so keep each conversation on whichever server it started on.

Before you start:
- Read config://organisation to discover severity IDs, custom field IDs, role IDs, and other values you'll need for filtering and grouping.
- Read playbook://analysis before doing any analytical or reporting work — it indexes all analysis playbooks and helps you pick the right one for the user's question. Then call analysis_start to download the playbook workspace.

Tool selection:
- analysis_start — call this BEFORE doing any analytical or reporting work (e.g. "analyse my incidents", "prepare for the review", "how are we doing?"). It downloads playbooks with step-by-step methodology, org config, and a branded HTML report template. Follow the playbook stages rather than ad-hoc querying — it produces much better analysis.
- stats tools (incident_stats, alert_stats, escalation_stats, follow_up_stats) — for counts, trends, and workload breakdowns across many records. Start here for analytical questions.
- list tools (incident_list, alert_list, etc.) — to browse or search individual records. Use the include parameter on incident_list to enrich results with roles or custom fields without calling incident_show for each one.
- show tools (incident_show, alert_show, etc.) — for full detail on a specific record. For investigation or root cause analysis, always request include: ["investigation", "postmor… [truncated]

{"id":"COR-1257","title":"go-nuts: embedded real-broker test suite — verify JetStream semantic beliefs against nats-server, not a fake","description":"## Problem

Every major bug found in the A1 review cycle was a **model error** — code faithfully implementing a wrong belief about JetStream semantics: Term doesn't settle on limits streams (<issue id="96688401-2b2d-48dd-8a77-a4400bd1bb45" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1492/entire-search-exhausted-ref-events-are-termed-which-does-not-settle">ENT-1492</issue>); `NumDeliver` increments on AckWait expiry with no handler involvement; the server stretches NAK delays by consumer BackOff increments; the last `backOff` rung tail-repeats under a larger `maxDeliver` (with an off-by-one — see <issue id="ef0f3a5a-67e4-48db-849c-8aafe12e38b0" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-1255/track-e-guardrails-and-cell-industrialization-admission-control">COR-1255</issue>); pedantic mode requires `ackWait = backoff[0]`. The unit suite runs against `natsmsgtest`'s fake, which encodes *the same model as the code* — so it stays green precisely when the model is wrong. The only step in the pipeline that consults reality is human review, which is why review keeps finding P1s.

## Proposed solution

An integration suite in go-nuts running an **embedded in-process nats-server** (pinned to the go.mod version), asserting every semantic belief the library encodes:

* ack-floor behavior with an unacked head-of-line message (floor stationary; later messages ack past it out of order)
* `NumDelivered` inflation on AckWait expiry / client death
* tail-repeat arithmetic: rungs served **before** delivery N, incl. the <issue id="ef0f3a5a-67e4-48db-849c-8aafe12e38b0" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-1255/track-e-guardrails-and-cell-industrialization-admission-control">COR-1255</issue> boundary cases
* capture-then-Ack settles and advances the floor; Term behavior on limits streams
* pedantic-mode rejections (`ackWait ≠ backoff[0]`, `maxDeliver ≤ len(backoff)`, stream `consumerLimits` interactions)
* regression assertions for **each P1 found in the current review rounds** (list from the review thread)

The fake (`natsmsgtest`) is demoted to library-logic tests only; the real-broker suite joins the merge gate. Also serves D0 bind-only later (expectations vs real `ConsumerInfo`) and <issue id="0a63017b-ca4e-4999-83c5-e558afcca5e1" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-1256/non-lossy-poison-message-break-glass-quarantine-nats-poison-ref-event">COR-1256</issue>'s quarantine tool (read-by-seq / publish / remove ordering); re-runs on every nats-server bump so upgrades re-verify the whole belief set instead of surprising us via incident.

**Acceptance:** suite green against embedded nats-server at the pinned version; every historical model-error P1 has an assertion; the A1 merge (<issue id="57d2a8d9-c2a6-49c4-8014-8a67857ef1b0" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1535/entire-search-the-ent-1492-dlq-doesnt-prevent-the-stall-a-poison-ref">ENT-1535</issue>) is gated on this helpers_test.go:11: natsserver "github.com/nats-io/nats-server/v2/server" connect_test.go:20: natsserver "github.com/nats-io/nats-server/v2/server" connect_test.go:195: // validation" — the documented nats-server test bypass. jsconsumer/jsconsumer_test.go:13: natsserver "github.com/nats-io/nats-server/v2/server" natsmsg/publish_test.go:10: natsserver "github.com/nats-io/nats-server/v2/server" ===DOC=== // Package nuts provides shared NATS connection-lifecycle helpers for Entire // services: a rotation-aware mTLS [Connect] with the org-standard resiliency // options, a [Drain] that waits for a connection to flush and close on graceful // shutdown, an [IsShutdownFetchErr] classifier so pull-consumer loops can treat // a drain/close during shutdown as a clean exit rather than an error, and a // [ShutdownGroup] that cancels background loops, joins them, and only then // drains the connections — the ordering that keeps a Drain from racing an // in-flight Fetch (COR-923). // // This root package is the connection-lifecycle core extracted from // entire-core (entiredb), entire-api, and mirror-pipeline, which had each // grown their own copy of this plumbing (COR-925). It depends only on nats.go. // // The subpackages carry the message-layer pieces those services shared // (COR-929, deepened in COR-984) — [natsmsg] (trace-context propagation over // message headers, the bounded deduped Publisher with a caller-selected // Operation span name, the KeepInProgress AckWait heartbeat, the DeadLetter // dead-letter capture, and the natsmsgtest.FakeMsg test double), // [jsconsumer] (the durable JetStream pull-consumer scaffold, one-shot via Start // or supervised via Run), and [backoff] (the NakWithDelay redelivery policy — // flat or growing — with Term-on-final-delivery, COR-762). The legacy // nats.JetStreamContext publishing bridges were transitional and were removed // once the last caller migrated (COR-1004). natsmsg and // jsconsumer additionally depend on the OpenTelemetry API, and all three on // nats.go's jetstream package; importing only the root package links none of // that. // // [natsmsg]: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/entireio/go-nuts/natsmsg // [jsconsumer]: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/entireio/go-nuts/jsconsumer // [backoff]: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/entireio/go-nuts/backoff package nuts ===README===

# go-nuts A small, dependency-light toolkit over [`nats.go`](https://github.com/nats-io/nats.go) for building [NATS](https://nats.io) and JetStream services in Go. The root package handles connection lifecycle — connecting, draining, and shutting down cleanly; opt-in subpackages add a durable JetStream pull-consumer scaffold, a publish helper, trace-context propagation, and a redelivery policy. ## Install ``` go get github.com/entireio/go-nuts ``` ## Connection lifecycle (root package) - **`Connect`** — dial with a resilient default posture: reconnect-forever (so a long-lived service rides out a NATS outage instead of permanently closing after the client's default 60 attempts), a bounded drain timeout, optional rotation-aware mTLS, and lifecycle log handlers that don't mistake a clean shutdown for a fault. Async errors (slow-consumer drops, permissions violations) and lame-duck notices are logged through the configured logger instead of nats.go's stderr default. - **`Drain` / `IsShutdownFetchErr`** — graceful shutdown. `Drain` starts nats.go's asynchronous drain and blocks until the connection flushes and closes (bounded by a timeout), returning an error and force-closing when it cannot complete; `IsShutdownFetchErr` lets a fetch loop treat a drain/close during shutdown as a clean exit rather than an error. - **`ShutdownGroup`** — cancels tracked background loops, waits for them to return, then drains the registered connections — the ordering that keeps a `Drain` from racing an in-flight `Fetch`. It owns disposition and delay calculation only (`NakOrTerm` over `jetstream.Msg`). MaxDeliver mirrors `jetstream.ConsumerConfig`: a non-positive value (`0` or `UnlimitedMaxDeliver`) means unlimited redeliveries, so bridge an unset `jsconsumer` consumer with its `EffectiveMaxDeliver()` rather than the raw field. ## Development Requires Go 1.26. 1	// Package jsconsumer is the durable JetStream pull-consumer scaffold shared by
2	// Entire's decode-and-dispatch consumers. Each of those used to hand-roll the
3	// same lifecycle: jetstream.New → CreateOrUpdateConsumer (durable, explicit
4	// ack, bounded ack-wait, bounded MaxDeliver, filter subject) → Consume → stop
5	// on context cancel; and the same per-message prologue: open a consumer span
6	// (re-parented across the NATS hop), decode the payload, and Term on a decode
7	// error.
8	//
9	// This package owns exactly that scaffold and nothing else. Each consumer
10	// keeps its OWN event type, business dispatch, metrics, and log lines — Start
11	// takes the consumer's message callback, and Process invokes the consumer's
12	// handle with the decoded event and the live span. The handler owns the
13	// message's terminal disposition (Ack/Nak/Term); Process never touches a
14	// message that decoded.
15	//
16	// Lifted from entire-api's internal/jsconsumer (COR-929), folding in the
17	// module's shutdown classification ([nuts.IsShutdownFetchErr] gates the
18	// consume-error log so a drain during rollout isn't reported as a fault,
19	// COR-923) and an optional [natsmsg.KeepInProgress] heartbeat for consumers
20	// whose handlers legitimately outrun AckWait.
21	package jsconsumer
22	
23	import (
24		"context"
25		"errors"
26		"fmt"
27		"log/slog"
28		"sync"
29		"time"
30	
31		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go"
32		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go/jetstream"
33		"go.opentelemetry.io/otel"
34		"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/codes"
35		"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace"
36	
37		"github.com/entireio/go-nuts"
38		"github.com/entireio/go-nuts/natsmsg"
39	)
40	
41	const (
42		// DefaultAckWait is how long JetStream waits for an ack before redelivery
43		// when Config.AckWait is zero — comfortably longer than an RPC round-trip
44		// plus a DB upsert, short enough that a stuck message redelivers promptly.
45		DefaultAckWait = 30 * time.Second
46		// DefaultMaxDeliver caps redelivery before JetStream stops redelivering a
47		// message when Config.MaxDeliver is zero.
48		DefaultMaxDeliver = 8
49	)
50	
51	// Config describes the durable consumer to create and how to trace/log it. The
52	// filter is given as either FilterSubject (single) or FilterSubjects (multi),
53	// mirroring jetstream.ConsumerConfig, so a migrated consumer preserves its
54	// existing on-server filter form exactly.
55	type Config struct {
56		Stream         string        // JetStream stream to bind (must already exist)
57		Durable        string        // durable consumer name, stable across restarts
58		FilterSubject  string        // set this OR FilterSubjects
59		FilterSubjects []string      // set this OR FilterSubject
60		AckWait        time.Duration // 0 → DefaultAckWait (see EffectiveAckWait)
61		MaxDeliver     int           // 0 → DefaultMaxDeliver (see EffectiveMaxDeliver)
62		SpanName       string        // per-message consumer span name (e.g. "repolifecycle.consume")
63		Name           string        // short consumer name, used as the log prefix
64	
65		// InactiveThreshold mirrors jetstream.ConsumerConfig.InactiveThreshold:
66		// how long the durable may go without an active subscription before the
67		// server deletes it; zero means never (the JetStream default for
68		// durables). Consumers on interest-retention streams set this so a
69		// decommissioned durable stops pinning every message it would have
70		// received, instead of holding them until the stream's MaxAge.
71		InactiveThreshold time.Duration
72	
73		// MaxAckPending mirrors jetstream.ConsumerConfig.MaxAckPending: the
74		// server-side cap on deliveries outstanding un-acked across ALL replicas
75		// sharing the durable; zero uses the server default (1000). Distinct
76		// from MaxMessages below, which caps only this process's client-side
77		// buffer.
78		MaxAckPending int
79	
80		// Tracer opens the per-message consumer span; nil uses the global OTel
81		// tracer provider.
82		Tracer trace.Tracer
83		// Logger receives the scaffold's own log lines (decode-term warnings,
84		// consume errors); nil uses slog.Default.
85		Logger *slog.Logger
86	
87		// KeepInProgress runs a natsmsg.KeepInProgress heartbeat while handle
88		// executes, for handlers that legitimately outrun AckWait. The extension
89		// is capped, so a wedged handler still redelivers — see
90		// natsmsg.KeepInProgress. The heartbeat stops when handle returns; a tick
91		// racing the handler's own terminal Ack/Nak/Term is a client-side no-op
92		// (nats.go marks the message disposed locally) that halts the heartbeat.
93		//
94		// Setting this forces the prefetch to one message (see MaxMessages): the
95		// heartbeat extends only the delivery the handler holds, so anything
96		// buffered behind a long handler would exhaust its AckWait unextended.
97		KeepInProgress bool
98	
99		// MaxMessages caps how many deliveries the consume loop buffers
100		// client-side (jetstream.PullMaxMessages); 0 uses the nats.go default
101		// (500). AckWait runs from server delivery into that buffer, not from
102		// callback dispatch, and callbacks run serially — so a consumer whose
103		// handler can approach AckWait should keep this small or queued
104		// deliveries expire and redeliver concurrently to other replicas.
105		// KeepInProgress forces it to 1; setting both to conflicting values is a
106		// Start error.
107		MaxMessages int
108	}
109	
110	// EffectiveAckWait is the AckWait actually applied to the JetStream consumer:
111	// Config.AckWait, or DefaultAckWait when zero. Use it — not the raw field —
112	// anywhere the real value matters, e.g. wiring a natsmsg.KeepInProgress
113	// heartbeat by hand (a zero ackWait there is a no-op).
114	func (c Config) EffectiveAckWait() time.Duration {
115		if c.AckWait == 0 {
116			return DefaultAckWait
117		}
118		return c.AckWait
119	}
120	
121	// EffectiveMaxDeliver is the MaxDeliver actually applied to the JetStream
122	// consumer: Config.MaxDeliver, or DefaultMaxDeliver when zero. Use it — not
123	// the raw field — when building a backoff.Policy for this consumer's
124	// messages: the two packages read zero differently (here it means "default
125	// to DefaultMaxDeliver"; on the policy it means unlimited redeliveries, the
126	// jetstream.ConsumerConfig semantics), so passing a zero Config.MaxDeliver
127	// through verbatim would make TermOnExhaustion never fire on the broker's
128	// real final delivery and orphan work-queue messages (COR-762).
129	func (c Config) EffectiveMaxDeliver() int {
130		if c.MaxDeliver == 0 {
131			return DefaultMaxDeliver
132		}
133		return c.MaxDeliver
134	}
135	
136	// validate rejects the configuration errors no retry can fix; shared by
137	// [Start] (one-shot) and [Run] (supervised, which must fail fast on these
138	// rather than retry them forever).
139	func (c Config) validate(nc *nats.Conn, onMsg func(jetstream.Msg)) error {
140		if c.KeepInProgress && c.MaxMessages > 1 {
141			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): KeepInProgress requires MaxMessages <= 1: the heartbeat extends only the in-flight delivery, so %d buffered messages would exhaust AckWait behind a long handler", c.Name, c.MaxMessages)
142		}
143		if c.Stream == "" {
144			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): Stream is required", c.Name)
145		}
146		if c.Durable == "" {
147			// CreateOrUpdateConsumer accepts an empty durable and silently makes
148			// an ephemeral, server-named consumer — losing the stable
149			// resume-across-restarts behavior this scaffold promises.
150			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): Durable is required", c.Name)
151		}
152		if onMsg == nil {
153			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): onMsg is required", c.Name)
154		}
155		if c.FilterSubject != "" && len(c.FilterSubjects) != 0 {
156			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): set FilterSubject or FilterSubjects, not both", c.Name)
157		}
158		for i, subject := range c.FilterSubjects {
159			if subject == "" {
160				return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): FilterSubjects[%d] is empty", c.Name, i)
161			}
162		}
163		if c.AckWait < 0 {
164			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): AckWait must not be negative", c.Name)
165		}
166		if c.MaxDeliver < -1 {
167			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): MaxDeliver must be -1 (unlimited), 0 (default), or positive", c.Name)
168		}
169		if c.MaxMessages < 0 {
170			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): MaxMessages must not be negative", c.Name)
171		}
172		if c.MaxAckPending < -1 {
173			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): MaxAckPending must be -1 (unlimited), 0 (server default), or positive", c.Name)
174		}
175		if c.InactiveThreshold < 0 {
176			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): InactiveThreshold must not be negative", c.Name)
177		}
178		if nc == nil {
179			return fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): nil nats conn", c.Name)
180		}
181		return nil
182	}
183	
184	func (c Config) tracer() trace.Tracer {
185		if c.Tracer == nil {
186			return otel.Tracer("github.com/entireio/go-nuts/jsconsumer")
187		}
188		return c.Tracer
189	}
190	
191	func (c Config) logger() *slog.Logger {
192		if c.Logger == nil {
193			return slog.Default()
194		}
195		return c.Logger
196	}
197	
198	// isShutdownConsumeErr reports whether a consume error is the benign result
199	// of the connection going away during shutdown. [nuts.IsShutdownFetchErr]
200	// covers the core nats.go sentinels, but the jetstream consume loop surfaces
201	// its OWN [jetstream.ErrConnectionClosed] — a distinct value that wraps
202	// neither — so it must be matched separately or a clean rollout drain still
203	// logs a warning (the COR-923 noise this suppression exists to remove). As
204	// with the root classifier, it is only "clean" when ctx is already done; a
205	// mid-run connection loss is a genuine fault worth logging.
206	func isShutdownConsumeErr(ctx context.Context, err error) bool {
207		return nuts.IsShutdownFetchErr(ctx, err) ||
208			(ctx.Err() != nil && errors.Is(err, jetstream.ErrConnectionClosed))
209	}
210	
211	// Runner is a live consume loop. Stop halts it and is idempotent.
212	type Runner struct {
213		cc jetstream.ConsumeContext
214		// closed is cc.Closed(), captured while the subscription is live (the
215		// same channel is returned on every call, so capturing once avoids any
216		// post-Stop race) — it closes when the consume loop has fully wound
217		// down, including an in-flight handler.
218		closed <-chan struct{}
219		// watcherDone closes when Start's context-cancellation watcher exits. It is
220		// intentionally internal: callers synchronize on Stop, while tests pin that
221		// an explicit Stop does not retain a goroutine until the parent context ends.
222		watcherDone <-chan struct{}
223		stop        sync.Once
224	}
225	
226	// Stop halts the consume loop and blocks until it has fully wound down —
227	// including an in-flight handler — so a caller may tear down what handlers
228	// use (stores, publishers, the NATS connection) the moment it returns: the
229	// cancel → join → drain shutdown ordering (COR-923). Safe on a nil or
230	// never-Started Runner, idempotent, and safe for concurrent use — an
231	// explicit Stop can race the context-cancel stop armed by Start. Must not be
232	// called from inside the handler; it would deadlock waiting on itself.
233	func (r *Runner) Stop() {
234		if r == nil || r.cc == nil {
235			return
236		}
237		r.stop.Do(r.cc.Stop)
238		<-r.closed
239	}
240	
241	// Start creates/updates the durable consumer on nc and begins delivering
242	// messages to onMsg, returning a Runner that Stops when ctx is cancelled. The
243	// stream must already exist (provisioned declaratively); callers whose cells
244	// opt in per-stream gate Start behind that opt-in so a cell without the stream
245	// doesn't error at CreateOrUpdateConsumer.
246	//
247	// Consume errors are logged at Warn, except a drain/close during shutdown —
248	// both the core nats.go sentinels ([nuts.IsShutdownFetchErr]) and jetstream's
249	// own connection-closed error — which is a clean exit rather than a fault.
250	func Start(ctx context.Context, nc *nats.Conn, cfg Config, onMsg func(jetstream.Msg)) (*Runner, error) {
251		if err := cfg.validate(nc, onMsg); err != nil {
252			return nil, err
253		}
254		js, err := jetstream.New(nc)
255		if err != nil {
256			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): jetstream.New: %w", cfg.Name, err)
257		}
258		cons, err := js.CreateOrUpdateConsumer(ctx, cfg.Stream, jetstream.ConsumerConfig{
259			Durable:           cfg.Durable,
260			AckPolicy:         jetstream.AckExplicitPolicy,
261			AckWait:           cfg.EffectiveAckWait(),
262			MaxDeliver:        cfg.EffectiveMaxDeliver(),
263			FilterSubject:     cfg.FilterSubject,
264			FilterSubjects:    cfg.FilterSubjects,
265			InactiveThreshold: cfg.InactiveThreshold,
266			MaxAckPending:     cfg.MaxAckPending,
267		})
268		if err != nil {
269			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): create consumer %s/%s: %w", cfg.Name, cfg.Stream, cfg.Durable, err)
270		}
271		consumeOpts := []jetstream.PullConsumeOpt{jetstream.ConsumeErrHandler(func(_ jetstream.ConsumeContext, cerr error) {
272			if isShutdownConsumeErr(ctx, cerr) {
273				return
274			}
275			cfg.logger().WarnContext(ctx, cfg.Name+": consume error", slog.Any("error", cerr))
276		})}
277		switch {
278		case cfg.KeepInProgress:
279			consumeOpts = append(consumeOpts, jetstream.PullMaxMessages(1))
280		case cfg.MaxMessages > 0:
281			consumeOpts = append(consumeOpts, jetstream.PullMaxMessages(cfg.MaxMessages))
282		}
283		cc, err := cons.Consume(onMsg, consumeOpts...)
284		if err != nil {
285			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): consume %s: %w", cfg.Name, cfg.Stream, err)
286		}
287		watcherDone := make(chan struct{})
288		r := &Runner{cc: cc, closed: cc.Closed(), watcherDone: watcherDone}
289		go func() {
290			defer close(watcherDone)
291			select {
292			case <-ctx.Done():
293				r.Stop()
294			case <-r.closed:
295			}
296		}()
297		return r, nil
298	}
299	
300	// isRetryableStartError classifies the narrow set of failures that can become
301	// healthy without changing Config or replacing nc. Everything else returns to
302	// the owner so a bad deployment cannot stay alive indefinitely with no
303	// consumer. Unknown server-side 5xx responses are retried, except known
304	// permanent JetStream configuration/account errors whose API happens to use a
305	// 5xx status.
306	func isRetryableStartError(err error) bool {
307		if errors.Is(err, jetstream.ErrStreamNotFound) ||
308			errors.Is(err, nats.ErrNoResponders) ||
309			errors.Is(err, nats.ErrTimeout) ||
310			errors.Is(err, nats.ErrDisconnected) {
311			return true
312		}
313	
314		var jsErr jetstream.JetStreamError
315		if !errors.As(err, &jsErr) || jsErr.APIError() == nil {
316			return false
317		}
318		apiErr := jsErr.APIError()
319		switch apiErr.ErrorCode { //nolint:exhaustive // unrecognized 5xx codes are deliberately retryable; all other unknown codes fail closed
320		case jetstream.JSErrCodeBadRequest,
321			jetstream.JSErrCodeConsumerCreate,
322			jetstream.JSErrCodeConsumerNameExists,
323			jetstream.JSErrCodeMaximumConsumersLimit,
324			jetstream.JSErrCodeJetStreamNotEnabledForAccount,
325			jetstream.JSErrCodeJetStreamNotEnabled,
326			jetstream.JSErrCodeConsumerAlreadyExists,
327			jetstream.JSErrCodeDuplicateFilterSubjects,
328			jetstream.JSErrCodeOverlappingFilterSubjects,
329			jetstream.JSErrCodeConsumerEmptyFilter,
330			jetstream.JSErrCodeConsumerExists:
331			return false
332		default:
333			return apiErr.Code >= 500
334		}
335	}
336	
337	// Retry envelope for [Run]'s supervision: exponential from runRetryInitial
338	// doubling to runRetryMax, reset once a consume loop survives longer than the
339	// max. Package vars (not consts) so tests can compress the schedule.
340	var (
341		runRetryInitial = time.Second
342		runRetryMax     = 30 * time.Second
343	)
344	
345	// Run supervises the consume loop [Start] builds. Where Start is one-shot —
346	// an error at consumer creation is returned, and a consume loop that closes
347	// underneath the caller (consumer deleted on the server, subscription
348	// invalidated) stays closed — Run retries both with exponential backoff
349	// (runRetryInitial doubling to runRetryMax, reset after a loop that outlives
350	// the max). In particular a stream that is not provisioned yet at boot — the
351	// declarative-provisioning race — is a retry, not a crash.
352	//
353	// Run blocks until ctx is cancelled, then joins the live loop (including an
354	// in-flight handler, see [Runner.Stop]) before returning, so it composes with
355	// the cancel → join → drain shutdown ordering as the body of a supervised
356	// goroutine:
357	//
358	//	g.Go(func(ctx context.Context) {
359	//		if err := jsconsumer.Run(ctx, nc, cfg, onMsg); err != nil {
360	//			log.Error("consumer config rejected", "error", err)
361	//		}
362	//	})
363	//
364	// Local configuration errors and permanent server responses (invalid consumer
365	// configuration, authorization/account setup) can never succeed on retry and
366	// are returned immediately. A missing declarative stream, temporary transport
367	// failure, or unknown server-side 5xx response remains supervised. A nil return
368	// means a clean, ctx-driven exit.
369	func Run(ctx context.Context, nc *nats.Conn, cfg Config, onMsg func(jetstream.Msg)) error {
370		if err := cfg.validate(nc, onMsg); err != nil {
371			return err
372		}
373		delay := runRetryInitial
374		for {
375			// Each attempt gets a child context so the cancel-watcher goroutine
376			// Start arms is released when the attempt dies, instead of one
377			// accumulating per recreate for the life of the process.
378			attemptCtx, cancelAttempt := context.WithCancel(ctx)
379			r, err := Start(attemptCtx, nc, cfg, onMsg)
380			if err != nil {
381				cancelAttempt()
382				if ctx.Err() != nil {
383					return nil //nolint:nilerr // a Start error during shutdown is a clean, ctx-driven exit, not a fault to report
384				}
385				if !isRetryableStartError(err) {
386					return err
387				}
388				cfg.logger().WarnContext(ctx, cfg.Name+": start consumer failed; retrying",
389					slog.Any("error", err), slog.Duration("retry_in", delay))
390			} else {
391				started := time.Now()
392				select {
393				case <-ctx.Done():
394					r.Stop()
395					cancelAttempt()
396					return nil
397				case <-r.closed:
398					cancelAttempt()
399					if ctx.Err() != nil {
400						return nil //nolint:nilerr // the loop closing during shutdown is the expected wind-down, not a fault
401					}
402					// A loop that ran long enough to be called healthy earns a
403					// fresh envelope; a flapping one keeps escalating.
404					if time.Since(started) >= runRetryMax {
405						delay = runRetryInitial
406					}
407					cfg.logger().WarnContext(ctx, cfg.Name+": consume loop closed; recreating",
408						slog.Duration("retry_in", delay))
409				}
410			}
411			select {
412			case <-ctx.Done():
413				return nil
414			case <-time.After(delay):
415			}
416			delay = min(delay*2, runRetryMax)
417		}
418	}
419	
420	// Process runs the per-message prologue shared by every consumer: open the
421	// consumer span (re-parented to the producer across the NATS hop), decode the
422	// payload, and on a decode error record it, log "<Name>: decode <Stream>;
423	// term", invoke onUndecodable (so the caller bumps its own drop metric with
424	// its own attributes), and Term the message — a poison payload won't decode on
425	// redelivery. On success it invokes handle with the span-enriched context, the
426	// live span (for RecordError/SetStatus on the business error paths), the
427	// message, and the decoded event; with Config.KeepInProgress set, an AckWait
428	// heartbeat runs for the duration of handle.
429	//
430	// Callers wire Process as the func they pass to Start AND the entry point
431	// their tests drive, so the decode-or-term path is exercised the same way in
432	// production and tests.
433	func Process[E any](
434		ctx context.Context,
435		msg jetstream.Msg,
436		cfg Config,
437		decode func([]byte) (E, error),
438		handle func(ctx context.Context, span trace.Span, msg jetstream.Msg, ev E),
439		onUndecodable func(ctx context.Context),
440	) {
441		ctx, span := natsmsg.StartConsumerSpan(ctx, cfg.tracer(), msg, cfg.SpanName)
442		defer span.End()
443	
444		ev, err := decode(msg.Data())
445		if err != nil {
446			span.RecordError(err)
447			span.SetStatus(codes.Error, "decode")
448			cfg.logger().WarnContext(ctx, cfg.Name+": decode "+cfg.Stream+"; term",
449				slog.Any("error", err), slog.String("subject", msg.Subject()))
450			if onUndecodable != nil {
451				onUndecodable(ctx)
452			}
453			if termErr := msg.Term(); termErr != nil {
454				cfg.logger().WarnContext(ctx, cfg.Name+": term failed", slog.Any("error", termErr))
455			}
456			return
457		}
458		if cfg.KeepInProgress {
459			stop := natsmsg.KeepInProgress(msg.InProgress, cfg.EffectiveAckWait())
460			defer stop()
461		}
462		handle(ctx, span, msg, ev)
463	}

1	// Package backoff is the redelivery policy for transiently-failed JetStream
2	// deliveries: a NakWithDelay envelope — flat by default, optionally growing
3	// multiplicatively per delivery — bounded by MaxDeliver, with an optional
4	// Term on the final delivery.
5	//
6	// The policy owns disposition and delay calculation only, and nothing wider:
7	// dead-letter capture, domain metrics/logging, and the decision of which
8	// failures are transient stay with the caller. It drives the modern
9	// [jetstream.Msg] API (NakOrTerm, NumDelivered, IsFinalDelivery).
10	//
11	// Delay calculation ([Policy.DelayFor]) is independent of message disposition:
12	// it is a pure function of the delivery count, so a caller can pin or meter the
13	// delay envelope without a message in hand.
14	//
15	// # Zero-value and unlimited semantics
16	//
17	// MaxDeliver matches [jetstream.ConsumerConfig.MaxDeliver]: a non-positive value
18	// (0 or [UnlimitedMaxDeliver]) means unlimited redeliveries, so no delivery is
19	// ever final and NakOrTerm always Naks. Note this reads zero differently from
20	// jsconsumer.Config.MaxDeliver, where 0 means "default to DefaultMaxDeliver":
21	// bridge with jsconsumer.Config.EffectiveMaxDeliver() (never the raw field), so
22	// an unset consumer MaxDeliver becomes the real default here instead of
23	// unlimited. Missing message metadata (a synthetic test message) reads as the
24	// first delivery — base NakDelay, never final — the safe default being another
25	// retry, not a Term.
26	//
27	// The Term-on-exhaustion posture is the COR-762 fix, lifted from
28	// mirror-pipeline's fanoutengine: on the final delivery a Nak is dropped
29	// silently by the broker (MaxDeliver reached), and on a WorkQueue stream the
30	// un-acked message then orphans — pinning the oldest-pending-age gauge — until
31	// StreamMaxAge finally expires it. Terming instead removes it cleanly. Streams
32	// where lingering is acceptable (a webhook stream whose max_age doubles as the
33	// retry backstop) leave TermOnExhaustion off and keep the plain Nak.
34	//
35	// Dead-letter capture stays with the caller, which should capture BEFORE
36	// disposing — gate it on [IsFinalDelivery]:
37	//
38	//	if backoff.IsFinalDelivery(msg, p.MaxDeliver) {
39	//		captureToDLQ(ctx, msg)
40	//	}
41	//	outcome, err := p.NakOrTerm(msg)
42	package backoff
43	
44	import (
45		"fmt"
46		"math"
47		"time"
48	
49		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go/jetstream"
50	)
51	
52	// UnlimitedMaxDeliver is the explicit Policy.MaxDeliver value for unlimited
53	// redeliveries (matching jetstream.ConsumerConfig.MaxDeliver, where a
54	// non-positive value disables the delivery cap). The zero value means the same
55	// thing; the named constant lets a caller say so on purpose.
56	const UnlimitedMaxDeliver = -1
57	
58	// Outcome is the disposition NakOrTerm chose, for the caller's metrics and
59	// logs.
60	type Outcome string
61	
62	const (
63		OutcomeNak  Outcome = "nak"
64		OutcomeTerm Outcome = "term"
65	)
66	
67	// Policy is the redelivery envelope a consumer applies to transient
68	// failures. MaxDeliver must match the consumer's on-server MaxDeliver — the
69	// policy detects the final delivery by comparing against it.
70	type Policy struct {
71		// NakDelay is the base delay before redelivery, and with a zero Factor
72		// the whole envelope: flat suits failures expected to clear on their own
73		// timetable, with MaxDeliver bounding the total.
74		NakDelay time.Duration
75		// Factor is the optional multiplicative growth per prior delivery: the
76		// Nth delivery naks with NakDelay × Factor^(N-1), capped at MaxDelay.
77		// Values ≤ 1 (including the zero value) keep the flat envelope. Growing
78		// envelopes suit failures that get cheaper to wait out than to retry —
79		// a downstream in a crash loop, a rate limit — where hammering on the
80		// flat cadence spends MaxDeliver too fast.
81		Factor float64
82		// MaxDelay caps the grown delay; it does nothing for a flat policy.
83		// Zero with a growing Factor leaves growth bounded only by MaxDeliver
84		// ending the redeliveries (the computed delay still saturates rather
85		// than overflowing).
86		MaxDelay time.Duration
87		// MaxDeliver is the consumer's redelivery cap
88		// (jetstream.ConsumerConfig.MaxDeliver). Non-positive (0 or
89		// UnlimitedMaxDeliver) means unlimited redeliveries — matching the
90		// jetstream field's semantics — so no delivery is ever final and NakOrTerm
91		// always Naks.
92		MaxDeliver int
93		// TermOnExhaustion makes the final delivery Term instead of Nak, so a
94		// work-queue message is removed cleanly rather than orphaning un-acked
95		// (COR-762). Callers with a DLQ capture before calling NakOrTerm.
96		TermOnExhaustion bool
97	}
98	
99	// NakOrTerm applies the policy to a transiently-failed [jetstream.Msg]
100	// delivery: NakWithDelay (see [Policy.DelayFor]) for redelivery, or — on the
101	// final delivery with TermOnExhaustion set — Term. Without TermOnExhaustion the
102	// final delivery still Naks; the broker drops the Nak at MaxDeliver and the
103	// stream's retention decides the message's fate.
104	//
105	// The returned Outcome reports which disposition was chosen, for the caller's
106	// metrics and logs. A disposition error is worth a log line but nothing more:
107	// a failed Nak redelivers via AckWait expiry anyway, and a failed Term on a
108	// work-queue stream means the message lingers exactly as it would have without
109	// the policy.
110	func (p Policy) NakOrTerm(msg jetstream.Msg) (Outcome, error) {
111		if p.TermOnExhaustion && IsFinalDelivery(msg, p.MaxDeliver) {
112			if err := msg.Term(); err != nil {
113				return OutcomeTerm, fmt.Errorf("term on final delivery: %w", err)
114			}
115			return OutcomeTerm, nil
116		}
117		if err := msg.NakWithDelay(p.DelayFor(NumDelivered(msg))); err != nil {
118			return OutcomeNak, fmt.Errorf("nak with delay: %w", err)
119		}
120		return OutcomeNak, nil
121	}
122	
123	// DelayFor reports the redelivery delay the policy applies after delivery
124	// number numDelivered (1 on first delivery): NakDelay for a flat policy,
125	// NakDelay × Factor^(numDelivered-1) capped at MaxDelay for a growing one.
126	// numDelivered ≤ 1 — including the 0 that [NumDelivered] reports when
127	// metadata is unavailable — reads as the first delivery. Exposed so a caller
128	// can log or meter the delay it is about to apply.
129	func (p Policy) DelayFor(numDelivered int) time.Duration {
130		if p.Factor <= 1 || numDelivered <= 1 {
131			return p.NakDelay
132		}
133		d := float64(p.NakDelay) * math.Pow(p.Factor, float64(numDelivered-1))
134		if p.MaxDelay > 0 && d >= float64(p.MaxDelay) {
135			return p.MaxDelay
136		}
137		if d >= float64(math.MaxInt64) {
138			// Uncapped growth outran time.Duration; saturate instead of wrapping
139			// negative (a negative NakWithDelay would redeliver immediately).
140			return math.MaxInt64
141		}
142		return time.Duration(d)
143	}
144	
145	// NumDelivered reports the JetStream delivery count of a [jetstream.Msg]
146	// (1 on first delivery), or 0 if metadata is unavailable (e.g. a synthetic test
147	// message).
148	func NumDelivered(msg jetstream.Msg) int {
149		if meta, err := msg.Metadata(); err == nil && meta != nil {
150			return int(meta.NumDelivered)
151		}
152		return 0
153	}
154	
155	// IsFinalDelivery reports whether this is the last delivery before JetStream
156	// stops redelivering (NumDelivered has reached MaxDeliver), so a transient
157	// failure here is terminal rather than another Nak-and-retry. A non-positive
158	// maxDeliver means unlimited redeliveries (the jetstream.ConsumerConfig
159	// semantics), so no delivery is final — without the guard the zero value
160	// would read every delivery as final and Term on the first failure.
161	// Unavailable metadata also reads as non-final: the safe default is another
162	// retry, not a Term.
163	func IsFinalDelivery(msg jetstream.Msg, maxDeliver int) bool {
164		if maxDeliver <= 0 {
165			return false
166		}
167		if meta, err := msg.Metadata(); err == nil && meta != nil {
168			return meta.NumDelivered >= uint64(maxDeliver)
169		}
170		return false
171	}

1	package natsmsg
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"fmt"
6		"strconv"
7		"time"
8	
9		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go"
10		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go/jetstream"
11	)
12	
13	// dlqPublishTimeout bounds one dead-letter PublishMsg. The consume context has
14	// no deadline, and PublishMsg waits for the PubAck indefinitely; without a
15	// bound a NATS blip would hang the handler (and, since a one-in-flight consumer
16	// keeps a slot occupied, stall the consumer) instead of failing the capture
17	// loudly.
18	const dlqPublishTimeout = 15 * time.Second
19	
20	// DLQ provenance headers added to the captured copy so a replay tool (or a
21	// human) can see why and from where a message was dead-lettered.
22	const (
23		DLQReasonHeader    = "Nats-Dlq-Reason"
24		DLQOriginHeader    = "Nats-Dlq-Origin-Subject"
25		DLQDeliveredHeader = "Nats-Dlq-Delivered"
26		DLQStreamSeqHeader = "Nats-Dlq-Stream-Seq"
27	)
28	
29	// DLQPublisher is the publish surface DeadLetter needs — the modern
30	// [JetStream] publish primitive (satisfied by jetstream.JetStream), aliased
31	// so DeadLetter's signature reads in DLQ terms. Kept minimal so wiring can
32	// hand it the same JetStream handle the per-cell publishers already hold,
33	// and tests can stub it.
34	type DLQPublisher = JetStream
35	
36	// SubjectToken sanitizes s into a single valid NATS subject token. NATS tokens
37	// cannot contain spaces, dots, or wildcards, so every character outside
38	// [a-z0-9_-] is replaced with '_' (and letters are lowercased). Use it to turn a
39	// human-readable dead-letter reason ("bad completion payload") into a subject
40	// token ("bad_completion_payload") — publishing to an unsanitized reason would
41	// fail, so the caller would never Ack the poison off a WorkQueue.
42	func SubjectToken(s string) string {
43		// Iterate bytes, not runes: we only keep ASCII [a-z0-9_-] and map everything
44		// else (including every byte of a multi-byte rune) to '_', so a byte loop is
45		// both correct and free of a rune->byte narrowing conversion.
46		b := make([]byte, 0, len(s))
47		for i := range len(s) {
48			c := s[i]
49			switch {
50			case c >= 'a' && c <= 'z', c >= '0' && c <= '9', c == '_', c == '-':
51				b = append(b, c)
52			case c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z':
53				b = append(b, c-'A'+'a')
54			default:
55				b = append(b, '_')
56			}
57		}
58		if len(b) == 0 {
59			return "unknown"
60		}
61		return string(b)
62	}
63	
64	// DeadLetter republishes a poison message to dlqSubject, preserving its payload
65	// and headers and adding Nats-Dlq-* provenance (reason, origin subject,
66	// delivery count, stream sequence).
67	//
68	// It is the capture step a consumer runs before giving up on a message it can
69	// never process. DeadLetter copies the poison to a durable DLQ subject so it can
70	// be inspected or replayed, and the caller then removes the original from the
71	// stream — a Term on the final delivery (see backoff.Policy.TermOnExhaustion,
72	// whose doc notes callers "DLQ capture before calling NakOrTerm") or a plain
73	// Ack. Without this step a Term'd or MaxDeliver-exhausted message is discarded
74	// with no trail; DeadLetter is what makes the give-up auditable and recoverable.
75	//
76	// Returns an error if the republish fails; on error the caller MUST NOT remove
77	// the original — Nak or leave it so the poison is never dropped without a
78	// captured copy. Publishing is bounded by dlqPublishTimeout regardless of ctx's
79	// deadline.
80	func DeadLetter(ctx context.Context, pub DLQPublisher, dlqSubject string, msg jetstream.Msg, reason string) error {
81		hdr := nats.Header{}
82		for k, v := range msg.Headers() {
83			hdr[k] = append([]string(nil), v...)
84		}
85		hdr.Set(DLQReasonHeader, reason)
86		hdr.Set(DLQOriginHeader, msg.Subject())
87		if meta, err := msg.Metadata(); err == nil && meta != nil {
88			hdr.Set(DLQDeliveredHeader, strconv.FormatUint(meta.NumDelivered, 10))
89			hdr.Set(DLQStreamSeqHeader, strconv.FormatUint(meta.Sequence.Stream, 10))
90		}
91	
92		out := &nats.Msg{Subject: dlqSubject, Data: msg.Data(), Header: hdr}
93	
94		pubCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, dlqPublishTimeout)
95		defer cancel()
96		if _, err := pub.PublishMsg(pubCtx, out); err != nil {
97			return fmt.Errorf("dead-letter publish to %q: %w", dlqSubject, err)
98		}
99		return nil
100	}

1	package nuts
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"log/slog"
6		"slices"
7		"sync"
8		"testing"
9		"time"
10	
11		natsserver "github.com/nats-io/nats-server/v2/server"
12	)
13	
14	// runEmbeddedServer starts an in-process NATS server on a random loopback port
15	// and returns its client URL. The server is shut down when the test ends.
16	func runEmbeddedServer(t *testing.T) string {
17		t.Helper()
18		return runEmbeddedServerWith(t, &natsserver.Options{}).ClientURL()
19	}
20	
21	// runEmbeddedServerWith starts an in-process NATS server from opts (host, port,
22	// and log/signal handling are forced to test-safe values) and returns the
23	// server handle for tests that drive server-side behavior such as lame duck
24	// mode. The server is shut down when the test ends.
25	func runEmbeddedServerWith(t *testing.T, opts *natsserver.Options) *natsserver.Server {
26		t.Helper()
27		opts.Host = "127.0.0.1"
28		opts.Port = -1 // pick a free port
29		opts.NoLog = true
30		opts.NoSigs = true
31		s, err := natsserver.NewServer(opts)
32		if err != nil {
33			t.Fatalf("new embedded nats server: %v", err)
34		}
35		go s.Start()
36		if !s.ReadyForConnections(10 * time.Second) {
37			t.Fatal("embedded nats server not ready in time")
38		}
39		t.Cleanup(s.Shutdown)
40		return s
41	}
42	
43	// capturingHandler is a thread-safe slog.Handler that records log messages so
44	// tests can assert what was logged, including from background goroutines.
45	type capturingHandler struct {
46		mu   sync.Mutex
47		msgs []string
48	}
49	
50	func (h *capturingHandler) Enabled(context.Context, slog.Level) bool { return true }
51	
52	func (h *capturingHandler) Handle(_ context.Context, r slog.Record) error {
53		h.mu.Lock()
54		h.msgs = append(h.msgs, r.Message)
55		h.mu.Unlock()
56		return nil
57	}
58	
59	func (h *capturingHandler) WithAttrs([]slog.Attr) slog.Handler { return h }
60	func (h *capturingHandler) WithGroup(string) slog.Handler      { return h }
61	
62	func (h *capturingHandler) has(msg string) bool {
63		h.mu.Lock()
64		defer h.mu.Unlock()
65		return slices.Contains(h.msgs, msg)
66	}
67	
68	func (h *capturingHandler) snapshot() []string {
69		h.mu.Lock()
70		defer h.mu.Unlock()
71		return slices.Clone(h.msgs)
72	}
73	
74	// waitFor blocks until a message equal to msg has been logged, or fails the
75	// test after a short deadline. Used to synchronize on logs emitted from a
76	// background loop goroutine.
77	func (h *capturingHandler) waitFor(t *testing.T, msg string) {
78		t.Helper()
79		deadline := time.Now().Add(2 * time.Second)
80		for time.Now().Before(deadline) {
81			if h.has(msg) {
82				return
83			}
84			time.Sleep(5 * time.Millisecond)
85		}
86		t.Fatalf("did not observe log %q; saw %v", msg, h.snapshot())
87	}
88	
89	// newCapturingLogger returns a logger writing to a fresh capturingHandler.
90	func newCapturingLogger() (*slog.Logger, *capturingHandler) {
91		h := &capturingHandler{}
92		return slog.New(h), h
93	}

1	package natsmsg
2	
3	import (
4		"errors"
5		"sync"
6		"time"
7	
8		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go"
9		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go/jetstream"
10	)
11	
12	// keepInProgressMaxTicks caps the total AckWait extension at ~5×AckWait
13	// (ticks fire at AckWait/3). The heartbeat exists so a long handler that IS
14	// making progress — a whole-installation teardown fan-out, a multi-GB
15	// data-plane purge — doesn't get redelivered into a concurrent duplicate;
16	// it must NOT remove the broker's liveness failsafe entirely, or a wedged
17	// handler (hung I/O with no deadline) would pin its delivery to the wedged
18	// replica forever. Past the cap the extension stops and AckWait expiry
19	// redelivers to a healthy replica sharing the durable.
20	const keepInProgressMaxTicks = 15
21	
22	// isPermanentInProgressErr reports whether an InProgress failure can never
23	// succeed on a later tick: the delivery was already terminally disposed (an
24	// Ack/Nak/Term racing the heartbeat) or carries no JetStream reply subject to
25	// extend. Both the jetstream and legacy *nats.Msg sentinel values are
26	// matched, since the callback may wrap either message type. Anything else —
27	// a reconnect-buffer overflow, a flush timeout — can recover once the
28	// connection does, so the heartbeat keeps trying until the tick cap.
29	func isPermanentInProgressErr(err error) bool {
30		return errors.Is(err, jetstream.ErrMsgAlreadyAckd) ||
31			errors.Is(err, jetstream.ErrMsgNoReply) ||
32			errors.Is(err, nats.ErrMsgAlreadyAckd) ||
33			errors.Is(err, nats.ErrMsgNoReply)
34	}
35	
36	// KeepInProgress calls inProgress at ackWait/3 until stop is called, resetting
37	// the broker's redelivery timer while a long handler runs. The extension is
38	// capped (keepInProgressMaxTicks) — see the constant for why.
39	//
40	// inProgress wraps the message's InProgress call — func() error { return
41	// msg.InProgress() } — for either jetstream.Msg or the legacy *nats.Msg.
42	//
43	// A failing tick stops the heartbeat only when the failure is permanent
44	// (already disposed, no reply subject — see isPermanentInProgressErr);
45	// a transient failure such as a NATS blip keeps ticking, bounded by the
46	// cap, so one dropped extension during a reconnect doesn't silently
47	// forfeit the rest of the handler's runway and invite a concurrent
48	// redelivery mid-run.
49	//
50	// A non-positive interval (zero ackWait on a hand-built consumer; real
51	// consumer configs default it) returns a no-op stop.
52	//
53	// stop is idempotent and blocks until the ticker goroutine has exited, so
54	// no InProgress can race a terminal disposition (Ack/Nak/Term) issued
55	// after it returns.
56	func KeepInProgress(inProgress func() error, ackWait time.Duration) (stop func()) {
57		interval := ackWait / 3
58		if interval <= 0 {
59			return func() {}
60		}
61		done := make(chan struct{})
62		finished := make(chan struct{})
63		go func() {
64			defer close(finished)
65			ticker := time.NewTicker(interval)
66			defer ticker.Stop()
67			for ticks := 0; ; {
68				select {
69				case <-done:
70					return
71				case <-ticker.C:
72					ticks++
73					if ticks > keepInProgressMaxTicks {
74						return
75					}
76					if err := inProgress(); err != nil && isPermanentInProgressErr(err) {
77						// A delivery that can't be extended won't start
78						// succeeding on a later tick; stop instead of
79						// spinning. The real failure surfaces on the
80						// terminal Ack/Nak/Term.
81						return
82					}
83				}
84			}
85		}()
86		var once sync.Once
87		return func() {
88			once.Do(func() { close(done) })
89			<-finished
90		}
91	}
92

IsShutdownFetchErr matched only ErrConnectionClosed and ErrConnectionDraining,
but a real drain rarely ends on one of those. A rolling pod restart mostly
produces ErrNoResponders, and a NATS server upgrade produces
ErrFetchDisconnected and ErrConsumerLeadershipChanged. Callers gated their
error log on the predicate, so every one of those was logged as a fault.

Measured on one mirror-pipeline deploy: a single pod emitted 57 ErrNoResponders
inside 83 milliseconds as its in-flight fetches failed together, and two
services between them crossed a cluster's error-log alert threshold three times
in forty minutes. The alerts were correct about the count and wrong about the
meaning, which is the failure mode that teaches operators to skim the one
signal that should mean something (COR-1226 / COR-1228).

Split the judgement in two. IsTransientFetchErr answers "is this recoverable",
independent of shutdown — a server rolling underneath a healthy caller produces
these while ctx is still live, so no ctx-based predicate can classify them.
IsShutdownFetchErr becomes exactly "transient AND ctx done", which widens it
correctly and leaves one list to maintain instead of two overlapping ones. A
test pins that relationship so the predicates cannot drift apart again.

ErrTimeout stays out: an idle poll reaching MaxWait is the steady state of a
quiet consumer, and callers already continue on it. context.DeadlineExceeded
stays out too — a slow server and a wedged one raise the same error, so
swallowing it would hide real stalls.

looping, reserving error for failures that stop recovering.

follow-up that retires its internal/natsmsg + internal/natsx.

{"id":"ENT-1535","title":"entire-search: the ENT-1492 DLQ doesn't prevent the stall — a poison ref event still pins the ack floor for ~18h before it dead-letters","description":"## Summary

<issue id="96688401-2b2d-48dd-8a77-a4400bd1bb45" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1492/entire-search-exhausted-ref-events-are-termed-which-does-not-settle">ENT-1492</issue> shipped the DLQ + `Ack()` fix so exhausted ref events stop leaking as unsettled `Term()`s. That fixed the *permanent* wedge and the silent data loss. It did **not** fix the stall that pages us.

On 2026-08-06 the same P1 fired again on `eks-prod-us-east-2`: one poison ref event pinned the `search-indexer-refs` ack floor for ~9h and search results went stale until a human manually deleted the message from the stream. The DLQ was still empty at the time of the page, because the retry ladder had not yet reached `MaxDeliver=7`.

**The gap:** the monitor fires at 50m of no floor movement, but the earliest the DLQ path can possibly run is **\~17h45m** after first delivery. Between those two points the consumer is stalled and nothing in the system recovers it. Dead-lettering is the right terminal behaviour; it is just far too late to be the stall remedy.

## Timeline (2026-08-06, all times UTC)

| Time | Event |

{"id":"ENT-1492","title":"entire-search: exhausted ref events are Termed, which does not settle them — dead-letter and Ack instead","description":"## Symptom

`search-indexer-refs` on `eks-prod-us-east-2` has had its ack floor pinned at stream sequence **2,601,158 since 2026-08-02 15:55:49Z** — ~40h as of writing. Delivery has advanced 74,000+ sequences past it. This is the second occurrence in three days (<issue id="97e263b0-2b6a-46a2-8630-1b6df08bc25e" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1479/entire-search-refsclaims-coordination-refs-are-indexed-as-content-pins">ENT-1479</issue> was the first, at 2,593,768).

The blocking message is `seq 2601159`: a `refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1` update on **Astrastellar/Jurialis** (`01KTB72G99A73334GEGXMHCP8B`), published 2026-08-01T22:54:37Z.

It was delivered 7 times over 24h, failed every time, and on the final attempt `settleFailure` took the terminal branch and called `msg.Term()` at **2026-08-03T16:22:56Z**. The floor did not move — not then, and not in the 15h since.

## Cause — Term is not a settlement on NATS 2.14.2

This is already documented in our own repo. From `fleet apps/nats-streams/base/repo-jobs-dlq-v1.yaml`:

> a message leaves the stream only on a positive Ack: **a Term or a MaxDeliver-exhausted Nak does NOT delete it (verified live in** <issue id="7cd52af2-3692-477e-8387-085db02250d7" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-944/repo-ops-v1-perms-sweep-termdmaxdeliverd-messages-leak-as-tombstones">COR-944</issue> **on NATS 2.14.2)**, so a poison / crash-orphaned job used to linger un-acked until its StreamMaxAge, pinning the queue and tripping the redelivery-floor alert (<issue id="73826c83-8078-490a-baf0-1fd8633c9573" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-960/dead-letter-orphaned-workqueue-jobs-analysis-index-streams-one-shared">COR-960</issue>).

We are on NATS 2.14.2 — confirmed from live stream info (`_nats.ver: "2.14.2"`).

`entire-search/internal/consumer/consumer.go:212` does exactly the thing <issue id="7cd52af2-3692-477e-8387-085db02250d7" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-944/repo-ops-v1-perms-sweep-termdmaxdeliverd-messages-leak-as-tombstones">COR-944</issue> established does not work:

```go
logger.Error().Err(err).Int("attempts", attempt).Str("action", "exhausted").
    Msg("ref event exhausted all retries")
_ = msg.Term()
```

Two problems in two lines:

1. `Term()` **does not settle the message**, so the ack floor stays pinned for tens of hours.

   Correction to the original wording here: it does eventually release. Two pins have now cleared on their own — this one at ~33h after the Term, and <issue id="97e263b0-2b6a-46a2-8630-1b6df08bc25e" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1479/entire-search-refsclaims-coordination-refs-are-indexed-as-content-pins">ENT-1479</issue>'s before it — **both without a redelivery and both *before* the message's retention deadline**. Seq 2601159 is still physically present in the stream and was never delivered an eighth time (117 log entries for that repo across the following day, all normal branch events). So this is a very delayed server-side reap, not a permanent wedge. Do not go hunting for something that never clears.
2. **The error is discarded.** If the call also failed we have no record either way.

Caveat worth verifying rather than assuming: <issue id="7cd52af2-3692-477e-8387-085db02250d7" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-944/repo-ops-v1-perms-sweep-termdmaxdeliverd-messages-leak-as-tombstones">COR-944</issue>'s finding is stated for **WorkQueue** streams, where the concern is the message leaving the stream. `repo_refs_v1` is `retention: limits`, so our symptom is the *consumer ack floor* rather than stream occupancy. The behaviours are consistent — Term is not treated as a settlement — but confirm that specifically before closing.

## Data loss, and there is no record of it

18 distinct checkpoints from Astrastellar/Jurialis were never indexed. With no DLQ, the only trace they ever existed is a comma-separated list inside one log line:

```
92c586c88029  3b96408c719d  d0bb908306d0  07277c6f3ee0  2003fd7d1a75
b228c3f086dc  352943bd29f2  f2c00342b735  dfaf8c2e9c90  4b8d7ebb3460
d708217c31e9  1c7b122001b8  fc9b463693be  8fb73b908cd0  28d2e357d313
9162560bd11c  98159c68a82c  e71630207ade
```

This is not isolated. **24 ref events were permanently dropped across all three prod cells between Jul 31 and Aug 4** — 23 of them eddacraft repos hitting `entiredb API error (status 500)` on `listing commit range`, most recently 2026-08-04T05:24:57Z. Every one silently discarded indexable content.

Those 23 fail in milliseconds and did *not* pin a floor, so the drop rate and the stall are separable: fast failures leave the floor alone, and only a long-running event pins it. Both stem from the same terminal branch.

## There is no operator escape hatch

Worth recording, because four routes were tried and all are walled off by design:

* `stream rmm repo_refs_v1 2601159` → `Permissions Violation for Publish to "$JS.API.STREAM.MSG.DELETE.repo_refs_v1"`. The natsctl identity carries per-message delete on the three enumerated DLQ streams only (`webhooks_github_dlq`, `repo_ops_dlq_v1`, `repo_jobs_dlq_v1`).
* Synthesising an ack by publishing to `$JS.ACK.…` → the natsctl identity has **no** publish verb at all, deliberately, so dead letters cannot be re-injected.
* Recreating the consumer → `consumerConfig()` sets no `DeliverPolicy`, so it defaults to `DeliverAllPolicy`. Deleting the durable and letting a pod recreate it would replay from `first_seq`: ~192,000 messages.
* `fleet docs/operator-guide/nats-operations.md` "Recover a wedged (poison-message) stream" does **not** apply — its own triage table routes "a stalled consumer pins interest, writes still succeed" away from that procedure. Following it would collapse a healthy R3 stream to one replica.

The only current remedy is waiting for `max_age` (96h) to age the message out — Aug 5 22:54:37Z for this one.

## The correct behaviour already exists one branch over

`settleFailure` has two terminal paths in the same `switch`, and only one of them works.

|  | transcript-pending | main (exhausted) |
| -- | -- | -- |
| ladder | 30s, 2m, 10m | 5m, 10m, 30m, 1h, 4h, 12h |
| max deliveries | 4 | 7 |
| **terminal action** | `msg.Ack()` | `msg.Term()` |
| floor outcome | advances within minutes | unsettled for tens of hours |
| data outcome | metadata-only index kept | event dropped, no record |

The transcript-pending branch says so in its own comment:

> `transcriptPendingMaxDeliver` = first attempt + one per backoff entry. **The terminal delivery ACKs** (the metadata-only index is durable), never NAKs.

Observed live on 2026-08-05, same consumer, same stream, same NATS 2.14.2 — about as clean an A/B as production offers:

* **Ack terminal.** Seq 2,716,494, a checkpoint event on Dropback/dropback (`01KTB89QK4XCQX1J0TETSKEHD1`). Three NAKs on the transcript-pending ladder from 01:38:34Z, terminal Ack on attempt 4, floor advanced 2,716,493 → 2,717,864 within minutes.
* **Term terminal.** Seq 2,601,159. Seven attempts, `msg.Term()` at 2026-08-03T16:22:56Z, floor pinned until roughly 2026-08-05T01:00Z.

So the fix is not a new pattern to design — it is making the exhausted branch consistent with its neighbour, with a dead-letter publish first so the event survives.

## Fix — copy the pattern that already works twice

`repo_ops_dlq_v1` (<issue id="7cd52af2-3692-477e-8387-085db02250d7" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-944/repo-ops-v1-perms-sweep-termdmaxdeliverd-messages-leak-as-tombstones">COR-944</issue>) and `repo_jobs_dlq_v1` solved this exact problem: republish the raw message to a DLQ, then **positively Ack** the original.

1. **Add** `repo_refs_dlq_v1` as a fleet stream manifest in `apps/nats-streams/`, copied shape-for-shape from `repo-jobs-dlq-v1.yaml`: `preventDelete: true`, `retention: limits`, `discard: new`, `storage: file`, `replicas: 3`, `maxBytes: 1 GiB`, `maxAge: 336h`, `duplicateWindow: 2m`, subjects `repo.refs.dlq.v1.>`.
2. **Change the terminal branch** in `settleFailure`: publish payload + headers + original subject to `repo.refs.dlq.v1.<reason>`, then `msg.Ack()`. Do not discard the publish error — if the dead-letter fails, NAK and let it retry rather than losing the event silently.
3. **Add** `repo_refs_dlq_v1` to the natsctl user's enumerated `STREAM.PURGE` / `STREAM.MSG.DELETE` grant in `apps/nats`. Additive, and it preserves the invariant that the carve-out only covers terminal streams — which is why granting delete on `repo_refs_v1` itself is the wrong move.
4. **Log the stream sequence** on every settle path (`msg.Metadata().Sequence.Stream`). Identifying seq 2601159 required joining an entiredb URL's `notRef`/`ref` query parameters back to a message body, because no log line names the sequence.

## Note for whoever picks this up

Since `repo_refs_v1` is `retention: limits`, an Ack does not delete the message — it only advances the consumer floor, and retention still ages it out at 96h. So unlike the WorkQueue cases there is no reaper needed here; the Ack alone is sufficient.

## Done when

* An exhausted ref event lands in `repo_refs_dlq_v1` with its payload, headers and original subject intact
* The ack floor advances past it immediately, verified live
* Term is gone from the terminal path, and no ack/publish error is discarded
* Every settle-path log line carries the stream sequence
* The 18 checkpoints above are replayed, or a decision is recorded not to
* Confirmed whether Term-does-not-settle applies to `limits` streams as well as WorkQueue, and <issue id="7cd52af2-3692-477e-8387-085db02250d7" So the fix is not a new pattern to design — it is making the exhausted branch consistent with its neighbour, with a dead-letter publish first so the event survives.

## Fix — copy the pattern that already works twice

`repo_ops_dlq_v1` (<issue id="7cd52af2-3692-477e-8387-085db02250d7" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-944/repo-ops-v1-perms-sweep-termdmaxdeliverd-messages-leak-as-tombstones">COR-944</issue>) and `repo_jobs_dlq_v1` solved this exact problem: republish the raw message to a DLQ, then **positively Ack** the original.

1. **Add** `repo_refs_dlq_v1` as a fleet stream manifest in `apps/nats-streams/`, copied shape-for-shape from `repo-jobs-dlq-v1.yaml`: `preventDelete: true`, `retention: limits`, `discard: new`, `storage: file`, `replicas: 3`, `maxBytes: 1 GiB`, `maxAge: 336h`, `duplicateWindow: 2m`, subjects `repo.refs.dlq.v1.>`.
2. **Change the terminal branch** in `settleFailure`: publish payload + headers + original subject to `repo.refs.dlq.v1.<reason>`, then `msg.Ack()`. Do not discard the publish error — if the dead-letter fails, NAK and let it retry rather than losing the event silently.
3. **Add** `repo_refs_dlq_v1` to the natsctl user's enumerated `STREAM.PURGE` / `STREAM.MSG.DELETE` grant in `apps/nats`. Additive, and it preserves the invariant that the carve-out only covers terminal streams — which is why granting delete on `repo_refs_v1` itself is the wrong move.
4. **Log the stream sequence** on every settle path (`msg.Metadata().Sequence.Stream`). Identifying seq 2601159 required joining an entiredb URL's `notRef`/`ref` query parameters back to a message body, because no log line names the sequence.

## Note for whoever picks this up

Since `repo_refs_v1` is `retention: limits`, an Ack does not delete the message — it only advances the consumer floor, and retention still ages it out at 96h. So unlike the WorkQueue cases there is no reaper needed here; the Ack alone is sufficient.

## Done when

* An exhausted ref event lands in `repo_refs_dlq_v1` with its payload, headers and original subject intact
* The ack floor advances past it immediately, verified live
* Term is gone from the terminal path, and no ack/publish error is discarded
* Every settle-path log line carries the stream sequence
* The 18 checkpoints above are replayed, or a decision is recorded not to

Stream invariants are enforced by comments (`webhooks_github_v1 maxAge ≥ 48h` vs the ~41h redelivery envelope); NATS users/grants are hand-written per cell — how five consumers shipped without `$JS.ACK` grants (<issue id="33e005d5-f925-4d4a-b46c-d423ec5ac549" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-1224/five-webhooks-github-v1-consumers-lack-an-explicit-dollarjsack-publish">COR-1224</issue>); monitors are hand-added per durable, so a consumer can ship unmonitored; deploys race the shared fleet branch with no ordering guard (a prod schema rollback already happened, <issue id="fbd6173d-349e-42f7-9a38-856d62fa4ef6" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-1046/deploy-pipeline-race-out-of-order-promotedeploy-lets-an-older-build">COR-1046</issue>); and the cell layer has zero fault-injection coverage — NATS is exempt in Antithesis, so every NATS failure mode has been discovered in production.

## Proposed solution

* **Admission control, three arms:** stream/consumer-CR invariant checks (maxAge vs ladder, DLQ pairing, limits); a NACK CR safety lint (require `preventDelete` + full-mirror specs, ban `inactiveThreshold`, block server-immutable edits, unique (stream, durable) per cluster); import-boundary lint — raw JetStream calls legal only inside go-nuts, ratcheted (grandfathered list only shrinks, named owner).
* promote↔deploy ordering gate (<issue id="fbd6173d-349e-42f7-9a38-856d62fa4ef6" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-1046/deploy-pipeline-race-out-of-order-promotedeploy-lets-an-older-build">COR-1046</issue>); strict up-to-date status checks on entire-api.
* Missing monitors: OTLP export failure (<issue id="715d583f-81ab-4119-b9ea-8606e8c10216" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-1085/no-monitor-on-otlp-metric-export-failure-delta-temporality-makes-a">COR-1085</issue>), entire-core log indexing (<issue id="b3e73f21-f13e-45e4-b769-b7ae67b6b913" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-1083/entire-core-logs-are-not-indexed-in-datadog">COR-1083</issue>), gateway 5xx (<issue id="209bcc59-9c5f-4907-a21d-2e1659431707" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-1099/gateway-generated-5xx-are-invisible-no-envoy-telemetry-and-app-side">COR-1099</issue>); runner_work monitors as GA gate.
* **Generate** NATS users, publish grants, and per-durable ack-floor monitors from the fleet Consumer CRs — the <issue id="33e005d5-f925-4d4a-b46c-d423ec5ac549" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-1224/five-webhooks-github-v1-consumers-lack-an-explicit-dollarjsack-publish">COR-1224</issue> class can't recur through this path.
* Fault injection to the cell layer: NATS as a fault target, entire-api in the Antithesis SUT; first chaos run exercises a NATS partition against a live consumer.

+// mechanism this suite does reproduce is
+// TestAckWithoutPublishPermissionSilentlySucceeds: a Term whose $JS.ACK publish

+// logged (COR-1224 found five consumers shipped without that grant).

14	// TestNonPositiveMaxDeliverMeansUnlimited pins the zero-value semantics both this
15	// module's packages document, from the only authority on them.
16	//
17	// A consumer created with MaxDeliver unset does not get "one delivery" or a server
18	// default cap: the server stores -1, unlimited redeliveries. That is the semantic
19	// backoff.Policy.MaxDeliver mirrors (non-positive means no delivery is ever final,
20	// so NakOrTerm always Naks), and the reason jsconsumer.Config.MaxDeliver reads 0 as
21	// DefaultMaxDeliver instead of passing it through: an unset field would otherwise
22	// silently become an unbounded retry ladder. Bridging the two conventions with
23	// EffectiveMaxDeliver() is what keeps TermOnExhaustion able to fire (COR-762).
24	//
25	// It also pins that unlimited is a WORKING configuration, not a rejected one — a
26	// MaxDeliver=-1 consumer starts and delivers — since "non-positive must be
27	// invalid" was itself one of the review's wrong beliefs.
28	func TestNonPositiveMaxDeliverMeansUnlimited(t *testing.T) {
29		t.Parallel()
30		nc, js := env(t)
31	
32		for _, tc := range []struct {
33			name    string
34			sent    int
35			wantOnS int
36		}{
37			{"unset becomes unlimited", 0, -1},
38			{"explicit -1 stays unlimited", -1, -1},
39			{"positive passes through", 3, 3},
40		} {
41			t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
42				cons := newConsumer(t, js, "events", jetstream.ConsumerConfig{
43					Durable:       "maxdeliver_" + tc.name[:6],
44					AckPolicy:     jetstream.AckExplicitPolicy,
45					MaxDeliver:    tc.sent,
46					FilterSubject: "events.repo",
47				})
48				if got := info(t, cons).Config.MaxDeliver; got != tc.wantOnS {
49					t.Errorf("sent MaxDeliver=%d, server stored %d, want %d", tc.sent, got, tc.wantOnS)
50				}
51			})
52		}
53	
54		// An unlimited consumer must actually run: this is the jsconsumer path a
55		// caller takes with MaxDeliver: -1 (UnlimitedMaxDeliver on the policy side).
56		t.Run("an unlimited consumer starts and delivers", func(t *testing.T) {
57			cfg := jsconsumer.Config{
58				Stream:        "events",
59				Durable:       "unlimited_durable",
60				FilterSubject: "events.repo",
61				Name:          "unlimited",
62				SpanName:      "test.consume",
63				MaxDeliver:    backoff.UnlimitedMaxDeliver,
64			}
65			if got := cfg.EffectiveMaxDeliver(); got != backoff.UnlimitedMaxDeliver {
66				t.Fatalf("EffectiveMaxDeliver() = %d, want %d passed through unchanged", got, backoff.UnlimitedMaxDeliver)
67			}
68			got := make(chan struct{}, 1)
69			run, err := jsconsumer.Start(t.Context(), nc, cfg, func(m jetstream.Msg) {
70				if err := m.Ack(); err != nil {
71					t.Errorf("ack: %v", err)
72				}
73				select {
74				case got <- struct{}{}:
75				default:
76				}
77			})
78			if err != nil {
79				t.Fatalf("Start with unlimited MaxDeliver: %v", err)
80			}
81			defer run.Stop()
82			publish(t, js, "events.repo", "hello")
83			select {
84			case <-got:
85			case <-time.After(waitTimeout):
86				t.Fatal("an unlimited-MaxDeliver consumer never delivered")
87			}
88			// And the policy built from it never calls a delivery final.
89			policy := backoff.Policy{MaxDeliver: cfg.EffectiveMaxDeliver(), TermOnExhaustion: true}
90			if policy.MaxDeliver > 0 {
91				t.Errorf("policy MaxDeliver = %d, want non-positive (unlimited)", policy.MaxDeliver)
92			}
93		})
94	}
95	
96	// TestJSConsumerDefaultsLandOnTheServer pins that the scaffold's documented
97	// defaults are the values the broker actually enforces.
98	//
99	// jsconsumer.Config's zero AckWait and MaxDeliver resolve to DefaultAckWait and
100	// DefaultMaxDeliver, and the doc for EffectiveMaxDeliver rests on the resolution
101	// happening BEFORE the config reaches the server — because an unresolved zero is
102	// unlimited there (see TestNonPositiveMaxDeliverMeansUnlimited), not 8. The fake
103	// cannot distinguish those two outcomes; the on-server config can.
104	func TestJSConsumerDefaultsLandOnTheServer(t *testing.T) {
105		t.Parallel()
106		nc, js := env(t)
107		cfg := jsconsumer.Config{
108			Stream:        "events",
109			Durable:       "defaults_durable",
110			FilterSubject: "events.repo",
111			Name:          "defaults",
112			SpanName:      "test.consume",
113			// AckWait and MaxDeliver deliberately unset.
114		}
115		run, err := jsconsumer.Start(t.Context(), nc, cfg, func(jetstream.Msg) {})
116		if err != nil {
117			t.Fatalf("Start: %v", err)
118		}
119		defer run.Stop()
120	
121		cons, err := js.Consumer(t.Context(), "events", "defaults_durable")
122		if err != nil {
123			t.Fatalf("look up consumer: %v", err)
124		}
125		got := info(t, cons).Config
126		if got.AckWait != jsconsumer.DefaultAckWait {
127			t.Errorf("on-server AckWait = %v, want DefaultAckWait (%v)", got.AckWait, jsconsumer.DefaultAckWait)
128		}
129		if got.MaxDeliver != jsconsumer.DefaultMaxDeliver {
130			t.Errorf("on-server MaxDeliver = %d, want DefaultMaxDeliver (%d) — a zero would have become unlimited",
131				got.MaxDeliver, jsconsumer.DefaultMaxDeliver)
132		}
133		if got.AckPolicy != jetstream.AckExplicitPolicy {
134			t.Errorf("on-server AckPolicy = %v, want explicit", got.AckPolicy)
135		}
136		// A policy built from the same Config agrees with the server about which
137		// delivery is final — the cross-package bridge, checked against the broker
138		// rather than against a fake's metadata.
139		if eff := cfg.EffectiveMaxDeliver(); eff != got.MaxDeliver {
140			t.Errorf("EffectiveMaxDeliver() = %d but the server enforces %d", eff, got.MaxDeliver)
141		}
142	}
143	
144	// REDACTED pins what happens to a consumer whose
145	// AckWait disagrees with its ladder's first rung — and that the answer depends on
146	// which client wrote it.
147	//
148	// On the ordinary client path (this module, nats.go's jetstream package) the server
149	// SILENTLY REWRITES AckWait to BackOff[0]. Nothing is rejected and nothing is
150	// logged, so a config review that reads AckWait from the manifest is reading a
151	// value the broker discarded — the ladder's first rung is the real ack timeout.
152	//
153	// The same mismatch IS rejected when the request sets pedantic mode, which NACK's
154	// controller does via jsm.go. So a fleet Consumer CR carrying this mismatch fails
155	// to reconcile in the cluster while the identical config applied from here succeeds
156	// quietly: a discrepancy worth pinning on both paths, since only one of them is
157	// exercised by the rest of this suite.
158	func REDACTED(t *testing.T) {
159		t.Parallel()
160		nc, js := env(t)
161		ladder := []time.Duration{time.Minute, 2 * time.Minute}
162	
163		t.Run("ordinary client path rewrites it", func(t *testing.T) {
164			cons := newConsumer(t, js, "events", jetstream.ConsumerConfig{
165				Durable:       "normalized",
166				AckPolicy:     jetstream.AckExplicitPolicy,
167				AckWait:       30 * time.Second, // disagrees with ladder[0]
168				BackOff:       ladder,
169				MaxDeliver:    5,
170				FilterSubject: "events.repo",
171			})
172			got := info(t, cons).Config.AckWait
173			if got != ladder[0] {
174				t.Errorf("on-server AckWait = %v, want it silently rewritten to BackOff[0] (%v)", got, ladder[0])
175			}
176		})
177	
178		t.Run("pedantic path rejects it", func(t *testing.T) {
179			apiErr := pedanticCreateConsumer(t, nc, "events", jetstream.ConsumerConfig{
180				Durable:       "pedantic_mismatch",
181				AckPolicy:     jetstream.AckExplicitPolicy,
182				AckWait:       30 * time.Second,
183				BackOff:       ladder,
184				MaxDeliver:    5,
185				FilterSubject: "events.repo",
186			})
187			if apiErr == nil {
188				t.Fatal("pedantic create accepted AckWait != BackOff[0], want a rejection")
189			}
190			if apiErr.ErrorCode != errCodePedantic {
191				t.Errorf("pedantic rejection err_code = %d, want %d (pedantic mode)", apiErr.ErrorCode, errCodePedantic)
192			}
193		})
